expectations.text: Cites a mean documentation quality of 67.11 percent measured across 2,529 public OpenAPI specs (OASQuali)
expectations.evidence: 'Mean documentation quality is 67.11% across 2,529 public OpenAPI specs.'

expectations.text: Cites parameter examples absent from 86.95 percent of specs
expectations.evidence: '86.95% of specs have no parameter examples.'

expectations.text: Labels the spec-corpus figures as peer-reviewed corpus measurement
expectations.evidence: Evidence quality column: 'Peer-reviewed'

expectations.text: Cites the Postman 2024 State of the API findings: 39 percent call inconsistent docs their biggest roadblock and/or 44 percent dig through source code to understand APIs
expectations.evidence: 39% inconsistent docs; 44% dig through source code.

expectations.text: Labels the Postman survey figures as large-sample survey self-report, distinct from spec measurement
expectations.evidence: 'Survey self-report'; 'The survey figures are perception.'

expectations.text: Presents the 1.7x to 56x faster time-to-first-call range as Postman's own vendor experiment, never as a controlled or independent result
expectations.evidence: 'Vendor experiment'; 'Neither figure is a controlled, independent result.'

expectations.text: Presents the roughly 10x faster and 225 percent registration figures as the Postman Moneris customer story, a named vendor case study
expectations.evidence: 'Postman, Moneris customer story, 2025 | Vendor customer story'

expectations.text: States that the try-it figures conflate the console with sandbox testing and better onboarding generally, so neither isolates the console's effect
expectations.evidence: 'It bundles the console with sandbox testing and better onboarding generally.'

expectations.text: Recommends measuring the company's own before-and-after time-to-first-call instead of reusing any vendor multiplier
expectations.evidence: 'Measure Corven's current time-to-first-call now... Report your own before/after figure.'

expectations.text: Does not present the roughly 10 percent undocumented-exception crash figure as a REST or HTTP API statistic; if cited at all it is attributed as an Android platform-API study
expectations.evidence: 'Do not cite the Kechagia 10% as a REST statistic. It is an Android platform study.'

expectations.text: If a time-to-first-call target appears, the under-10-minutes bound is labeled practitioner consensus, not a measured industry statistic
expectations.evidence: 'practitioner consensus bound... a borrowed target, not an industry average.'

expectations.text: Every figure presented carries a named source rather than appearing as an unattributed statistic
expectations.evidence: Each table row names a source.

expectations.text: Positions Stripe and Twilio as practitioner-consensus benchmarks compared by checkable mechanisms, not as controlled comparison evidence
expectations.evidence: Only Stripe is mentioned ('Stripe's docs embed live, personalized test keys'). Twilio is not positioned as a benchmark.
